blocks.heading: It Depends Entirely on the Field

figures.label: Total Course Duration
figures.source: It depends entirely on the field, the university tier, and how you fund it. An MS in computer science, data science, or engineering from a well-ranked public university, funded mostly through savings or a manageable loan, still produces a strong return for most students within 3-6 years of working in the US or returning to India with US experience. An MS in a saturated field, from a low-ranked university, funded entirely through high-interest debt, is a weak bet, the degree cost and the H1B uncertainty combine to create real financial risk that a general "worth it" answer cannot capture.

figures.label: Total Education Cost
figures.source: All-in, over roughly two years, expect Rs 60-80 lakh at budget public universities in lower-cost cities, Rs 95 lakh to Rs 1.25 crore at mid-range public universities in bigger cities, and Rs 1.4 crore to Rs 1.8 crore or more at private and Ivy-tier universities in expensive metros. This includes tuition, housing, food, health insurance, and visa costs, not just the tuition figure shown on a university brochure.

items.text: Your field (commonly computer science, data science, certain engineering specializations) has strong, verifiable US employer demand at the OPT stage, not just at the H1B stage.
You can fund most of the cost through savings, assistantships, or scholarships, keeping loan exposure to an amount your family can absorb even in a no-H1B outcome.
You have already checked that the specific university and program you are targeting places graduates into roles that match the earning ranges above, not just a general "top ranked" reputation.

You have a real answer for what you do professionally if you return to India after OPT, the US degree and work experience still needs to translate into a stronger India-based role, not just a stronger visa story.
